issues.title: Extension bound uses the wrong source domain

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Here, we assume the existence of a bounded map $\mathcal{R}\colon V^+\rightarrow V^-$

issues.failure_explanation: The paper defines R as a map from the positive-side space to the negative-side space and quantifies the lemma over w in V(Omega+). Its first bound nevertheless uses the target domain Omega- on both sides. The right-hand gradient norm is therefore not a norm of the stated input, unlike the immediately adjacent L2 bound, which correctly uses Omega+ as its source domain.
issues.overall_effect: As printed, the H1 operator norm of R is undefined for the stated inputs. This leaves the energy bounds for T and the subsequent coercivity, decay, inf-sup, and error-estimate chain without a valid source-to-target extension constant.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the first bound in eq:norm1 of R to ||∇Rw||_{Omega-} <= ||R||_1 ||∇w||_{Omega+}, interpreting ||R||_1 as the H1 source-to-target operator bound. Use this corrected bound throughout the listed coercivity, decay, inf-sup, and error arguments without otherwise changing them.
issues.why_classification: The declaration R:V+→V−, the quantifier w∈V(Omega+), and the adjacent L2 estimate uniquely force Omega+ on the right. The printed Omega− norm is ill-typed, and its uniquely determined transcriptional correction changes no inference or mathematical guarantee.

issues.title: Global basis construction has the wrong test-space interface

diagnostic_evidence.quote: by using the fact in \cref{msbasis}, it is easy to obtain the first argument.

issues.failure_explanation: The construction declares phi_i^j to be a global member of V but supplies its variational equations only for w in V(K_i), even though B is defined on V by global integrals. This leaves the function outside K_i unconstrained or makes the test argument inadmissible. It therefore cannot imply B(v_glo,w)=0 for every global w in the projection kernel. Although the old analysis later introduces an all-V operator G_i^infinity, it never identifies the previously declared V_glo with that operator's image.
issues.overall_effect: The global Galerkin space is not connected to the operator used by the analysis, so global orthogonality, membership of the global error in the kernel space, the global estimate, and the subsequent local inf-sup transfer are not established for the declared construction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the test condition w∈V(K_i) in msbasis by w∈V. Since each psi_i^j is zero-extended and fixed by pi, identify phi_i^j=G_i^infinity psi_i^j and, by expansion in the auxiliary basis, V_glo=Im(G^infinity). This restores lm3.2, the kernel characterization of the global error, and the listed downstream estimates.
issues.why_classification: The construction and global orthogonality genuinely fail under the printed test interface, so this is not merely a typo. Nevertheless, the old source already supplies the corresponding all-V operator, and one routine test-space correction plus a finite-dimensional linearity identification repairs the entire affected chain with no new lemma, method change, or loss of guarantee.

issues.title: Global error theorem omits C1/epsilon_0
issues.failure_explanation: The theorem claims the estimate with coefficient one. Its first proof inequality divides the coercivity estimate by epsilon_0, while the source pairing is bounded using C1. Carrying those factors through and dividing by the error norm gives C1/(epsilon_0 sqrt(Lambda)), not 1/sqrt(Lambda). No old assumption identifies C1 with epsilon_0 or bounds their ratio by one.
issues.overall_effect: The exact global energy estimate is stronger than its proof supports by the multiplicative factor C1/epsilon_0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State glothm as ||u-u_glo||_a <= C1 ||f||_{s^{-1}}/(epsilon_0 sqrt(Lambda)) and retain the factor 1/epsilon_0 when the proof replaces the bilinear form by the source pairing.
issues.why_classification: This is a genuine dropped-factor inference rather than a purely typographical malformed expression. Tracking the two already defined stability constants is short and routine, and it changes neither the theorem's hypotheses nor its Lambda rate, norm, or applicability.

issues.title: Cea proof uses a different localized multiscale space

failure_location.quote: First, for any $u_{\mathup{ms}}\in V_{\mathup{ms}}$, we can find $\psi$ such that $u\in V_{\mathup{ms}}=\hat{\mathcal{G}}^m\psi$.

issues.failure_explanation: The old definition makes V_ms the span of basis functions solving msbasis1 on the ordinary patches K_i^m. The Cea proof instead assumes V_ms equals the image of the modified operator hat G^m on the generally different symmetric patches hat K_i^m. No equality or transfer map between these two spaces is established, so the proof's inf-sup transfer and comparison functions do not apply to the declared Galerkin space.
issues.overall_effect: Inf-sup stability and quasi-optimality are not established for the multiscale space actually declared before cemvar, and consequently the main existence, uniqueness, and error conclusions for that space are unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For each fixed oversampling level m, define the analyzed space by V_ms=Im(hat G^m), equivalently as the span of hat G_i^m psi_i^j on the symmetric patches, and formulate cemvar on that space. State Cea and the main theorem for this symmetric-patch method; do not claim them for the original ordinary-patch space without a separate equality or transfer proof.
issues.why_classification: The ordinary-patch space is coherently defined and is generally not equal to the symmetric-patch image, so changing the definition alters the algorithmic construction and exceeds a minor repair. However, the old source already develops the decay and inf-sup machinery for the symmetric-patch space, yielding a recognizably comparable method with the same central estimate through a contained redefinition rather than global proof reconstruction.

issues.title: Unsupported wavenumber decay in the main error estimate

failure_location.quote: For $I_1$, we utilize the global error estimate \cref{glothm}, and for the constant $C_1$, we use the resolution condition \cref{eq:res} again to obtain the estimate that $C_1$ depends on $k^{-1}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem claims a leading k^{-1}/sqrt(Lambda) term, and its proof says that the resolution condition makes C1 depend on k^{-1}. In the old source, however, C1 is defined solely through the extension-operator bound and Upsilon and is bounded below by sqrt(2). The resolution condition only restricts admissible combinations of k, H, and Lambda; it does not redefine C1 or imply C1=O(k^{-1}). Thus the displayed derivation supplies a C1 stability factor, not the claimed k^{-1} factor.
issues.overall_effect: The favorable k^{-1} wavenumber scaling advertised by the main a priori estimate is not established, although the H-dependent localization term is unaffected by this root.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the assertion that the resolution condition makes C1 proportional to k^{-1}. Replace the leading k^{-1}/sqrt(Lambda) contribution by the stability-factor contribution actually inherited from the global estimate, proportional to C1/(epsilon_0 sqrt(Lambda)), absorbing these constants into C_cem if desired but claiming no k^{-1} decay. Retain the localization term unchanged.
issues.why_classification: C1 is independent of k and bounded below by sqrt(2), so the advertised wavenumber decay has no source-supported local proof. Withdrawing that decay is a substantive rate weakening and therefore not minor, but the same method and a recognizably comparable a priori estimate with unchanged Lambda and localization behavior survive by a contained edit, so the loss is not major.

issues.title: Oversampling threshold leaves a logarithmic loss

failure_location.quote: In particular, if $m\geq 4|\mathup{log} (H)|/|\mathup{log} (\theta)|$, then we have optiaml order convergence in $H$; i.e., it holds that

issues.failure_explanation: Let L=|log H| and t=|log theta|. At the allowed choice m approximately 4L/t, theta^{(m-1)/2} is a constant multiple of H^2. Hence the localization factor H^{-2}(m+1)^{d/2}theta^{(m-1)/2} is of order |log H|^{d/2}, not O(1). Since the old source states that the source norm is O(H), the resulting estimate is only O(H|log H|^{d/2}) at the threshold, rather than the asserted uniform O(H).
issues.overall_effect: The theorem's explicit oversampling condition does not establish its claimed optimal H-order; it leaves a polylogarithmic loss.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the explicit sufficient condition to m >= (4+delta)|log H|/|log theta| for any fixed delta>0, with integer rounding and sufficiently small H. Then H^{-2}(m+1)^{d/2}theta^{(m-1)/2}=O(H^{delta/2}|log H|^{d/2})=O(1), which restores the asserted O(H) conclusion while retaining logarithmic oversampling.
issues.why_classification: Accounting for the displayed polynomial factor requires only an elementary local estimate and a harmless constant-factor increase in the oversampling level. The method, model class, convergence rate, and asymptotic m=O(|log H|) complexity are preserved. It is not a typo because the printed inference is false and the correction is not uniquely transcriptional.
